architecture: v2 (re-root 2026-10-31: an integrated care board's split of its 2027 Heat Resilience Fund among its six places by each place's excess deaths in June to August 2026, the deaths that occurred whether registered yet or not, completed from the medical examiner offices' log of deaths the coroner holds for inquest)
slot_note: batch 1 re-root; architecture 1 (quantitative finance, the 13F holdings carry) failed the portal's determinism block and the survivor anatomy
niche: provisional deaths by date of occurrence for a heat summer, completed for the deaths a coroner's inquest keeps off the register by linking the medical examiner offices' referral log to the registrations
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads every field and the fund's rule correctly counts each place's residents' deaths with a June to August 2026 date of death on the register as extracted in October and completes them with the share of earlier summers' deaths registered by the same point, which reproduces every earlier summer's final count; this summer's unregistered deaths were not the usual few, because the July heat wave's deaths of people found at home went to the coroner and the north coroner opened inquests on them, so the earlier summers' completeness understates Ashwold and overstates the places whose deaths were all registered.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each place's deaths by date of occurrence, the vital-statistics series a provisional registration extract understates by its registration lag and that official mortality series complete before they are used; the lag is long only for deaths a coroner holds for inquest, so the count is completed from the medical examiners' referral log, and swapping in another field's records (admissions, claims, sales) loses the coroner's hold that makes the lag.
layer1: a registration extract with amended registrations as second rows
dates in two formats either side of the register's 2023 system change
residents' deaths registered in other districts
the deceased's name in one field in the referral log and in two fields on the register
two medical examiner offices' logs with different layouts
postcodes placed in places through a lookup that holds terminated postcodes
UTC timestamps on one office's case system
stakeholder_role: the integrated care board's heat resilience panel

spine.entity: a death registration (an amendment is a second row)

world.geography: England (a fictional integrated care board area of six local authority places)
world.org_type: an NHS integrated care board's population health intelligence team

driver: A count by date of occurrence for a recent window is completed for the units a second body still holds out of the record, read from that body's own log linked to the record on personal identifiers and dates, because the usual completion factor assumes the hold is as rare as in the closed windows it reproduces.
driver_concrete: Each place's summer 2026 deaths are the deaths on the register plus the deaths the medical examiners referred to the coroner on which an inquest is still open, linked by name, birth date and date of death and placed by the deceased's postcode, because the July heat wave sent the deaths of people found at home to the coroner, so the earlier summers' share registered by October understates the summer and only the referral log names the missing deaths.
stump: A competent analyst completes each place's registered summer deaths with the earlier summers' share registered by the same point and splits the fund on the excess; the step that lands it there is treating this summer's unregistered deaths as the usual few, when the north coroner holds the heat wave's deaths at home for inquest and Ashwold's are most of them.

differentiation.task107: task107 v3-etl re-pointed a payroll pipeline at a payments-only feed, so one file's window silently dropped each person's nil months; here no file is wrong and nothing is dropped: the deaths missing from the register are complete records in another body's log, held there by an inquest, and are found only by linking that log to the register on name, birth date and date of death.
differentiation.task181: task181 completes specimens notified against collected with each courier route's own delay (a nowcast by route); here no delay is estimated at all: the deaths the register lacks are named one by one in the medical examiners' referral log, so the golden is an enumeration through a link, and every delay model, pooled or by place, is a rung below it.
differentiation.task485: task485 carries arrivals' retention from earlier arrivals conditioned on each arrival's own migration history; here nothing is carried from earlier cohorts: the earlier summers' completeness is the wrong rung, and the count is completed from a second body's log of the deaths it still holds.

lineage.fate: in-house round 2 missed at flat carry; in-house round 3 (2026-10-11) landed the call on the register-type change pooled across the names (0.042 points in OM-4 s.2's back-test against 0.60 for the all-filer change); hardened in loop 2 by making the index sponsors' holdings follow each name's share count, so that basis is the stump rung
lineage.driver: A period still open at the extract is completed for the reporters not yet in by carrying each from its last report, but that report is stale for the class of reporter whose holdings drift every period at a common rate, so each missing reporter is moved by the drift its own class already shows among those that have reported, the basis a filed back-test criterion selects; flat carry misplaces the unit whose missing reporters are of the drifting class, and any single rate for every missing reporter misplaces the unit whose missing reporters are not.

lineage.fate: portal round 1 (2026-10-11): rubric average 52, determinism QC failed (answer_contradicts_files, golden_wrong): OM-4 s.2 named the filers for the period and filed no completion, so the literal reading counted only the reports on file; the driver also collided with task181 (task446 pre-flight); hardened in loop 1 by filing the estimand and a basis-selection criterion and moving the decisive step to the basis
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is the part of a period's total still held by reporters whose reports have not arrived at the extract; because slow reporters concentrate in some units and not others, it has to be completed reporter by reporter from each one's last report, and reading the arrived reports as the total, or scaling every unit by one aggregate completion share, misstates exactly the units whose holders report late and changes which units cross the threshold.

lineage.niche: an independent ownership-research firm's quarterly crowded-ownership flag on a client watchlist, set from the SEC Form 13F structured data sets while the quarter's filing window is still open, so the flag has to rest on the institutional ownership the completed filing set will show
lineage.driver: One class of holder keeps a fixed fraction of each unit rather than a fixed amount, so when a unit's size changes that class's amount in it moves with it, and the class's common change is a change in the fraction, the same in every unit; completing the holders not yet reported in a still-open period with one amount change per class pooled across units misstates the units whose size moved, carrying every class as a fraction misstates the units whose missing holders keep amounts, and the basis a filed back-test criterion selects moves each missing holder of that class with its own unit's size and the class's change in fraction while every other class keeps its amount.
lineage.stump: A competent solver executes OM-4 literally, sees that the index and ETF sponsors that have filed grew their share holdings while every other register type held flat, grows each of the 129 managers still due by its own type's change pooled across the twelve names, sees that basis beat every other it builds in the September back-test (largest miss about 0.66 points against 1.0 for the all-filer change, 1.4 for flat carry and 2.2 per name), and flags WHII, GLI, JEMS and SAF with OTF at about 79.2; the step that lands it there is treating the sponsors' change as one factor for every name, when an index sponsor holds a fixed slice of each company, so in shares it moves with that name's share count as well as with its creations: OTF issued about 4.6 per cent more shares in October and its sponsors still due, 23 per cent of OTF, took their slice, which the two filed sponsors' OTF holdings show (up about 10.4 per cent against 4.5 pooled), so the basis the filed criterion selects grows each sponsor still due by the change its filed peers show in that name (largest miss about 0.04), which puts OTF at 80.4 and keeps FENN, whose managers still due are multi-strategy funds, at 79.6.
